##  Uncertainty analysis.

The large variability of seismic hazard must be considered in design scenarios with a high degree of consequences to failure. The PSHA study prepared by LCI, has reported seismic intensities and annual exceedance probabilities for seven fractiles (5%, 10%, 16%, 50%, 84%, 90% and 5%) that allow estimating the variability of seismic hazard for a given service level. Assuming a log-normal distribution <ID.F417E99A> for the seismic intensities of a given service level, the dispersion between the 16% and 84% percentiles allows estimating the standard error of the hazard model, according to <ID.0B535788> and the mean value <ID.5DC4E7CA>. 

If <ID.B3694F92> is the median (50%) of some seismic intensity measure, the 84% percentile of this measure can be estimated from <ID.8DDAFFA9> and this expression can be used to estimate the variability of any seismic design parameter based on that intensity measure, assuming that they have a log-normal distribution and an approximately linear relationship with the seismic intensity.
